newsitem.title: MALTA: Malta tourism dips but appears to be recovering.
newsitem.headline: Malta tourism dips but appears to be recovering.

text.p: Tourism to the Mediterranean island of Malta fell by 0.4 percent in August, but government officials said it appeared that the industry was starting a recovery after steeper drops earlier this year.

Malta's Central Office of Statistics said on Thursday that arrivals had increased from Germany, Malta's second biggest market, as well as the Netherlands, Scandinavia, the United States and Libya. There were drops from Britain -- the biggest market -- and Italy, France, Belgium and Austria.

Prime Minister Eddie Fenech Adami told an election campaign news conference earlier that gross earnings from tourism in the first seven months of this year reached 121.5 million Maltese lira ($334 million) compared to 122.4 million in the same period last year.
Tourism arrivals dropped by almost 10 percent in March and April but arrivals start picking up again in May and June.
Figures for July were almost unchanged from the same month in 1995. Fenech Adami said the outlook for October to December appeared to be "very good."
